title: Combination Sum II
prompt:
Given `candidates` (which may contain duplicates) and a `target`, return all unique combinations whose values sum to `target`. Each element may be used **at most once**, and the result must not contain duplicate combinations.

**Example**: `candidates = [10,1,2,7,6,1,5]`, `target = 8` → `[[1,1,6],[1,2,5],[1,7],[2,6]]`.

**Constraints**: 1 ≤ candidates ≤ 100, 1 ≤ candidates[i] ≤ 50, 1 ≤ target ≤ 30.
hints: There are two separate issues: each element can be used once, and duplicate values would create repeated combinations. Which earlier technique deals with duplicate values?
Sort, then backtrack with `(start, remaining)`, recursing with `i + 1`. Record a copy when `remaining == 0`.
Skip repeated values in the same loop with `if (i > start && candidates[i] == candidates[i - 1]) continue;`. Because the array is sorted, `break` once `candidates[i] > remaining`.

solution.explanation: Recursing with `i + 1` limits each element to one use, and the same-loop skip means the two 1s produce `[1,7]` only once while `[1,1,6]` can still use both. Sorting also means that once one candidate is too large, all later ones are too, so the loop can stop. O(2ⁿ) time worst case, O(n) recursion depth.
